The duelists

Same champion. Same spells.

Game 5 was played in blind pick, so both mid laners could lock in Zed. SKT are sieging KT's base with a 13k gold lead, but in this corner of the map it's a straight one-on-one, and it starts on Ryu's terms.

Faker

SK Telecom T1 K · Mid
  • Classic Zed: the crimson one
  • Level 18 · Flash + Ignite
  • Holding Quicksilver Sash
  • 17 years old, in his rookie season
VS

Ryu

KT Rolster Bullets · Mid
  • Shockblade Zed: silver, cyan lightning
  • Level 16 · Flash + Ignite
  • 1,930 max HP · 249 attack damage
  • Fighting inside his own base

In every frame below, a red tag marks Faker and a blue tag marks Ryu. You can toggle the tags off in the frame-by-frame header to see the raw broadcast.

Rules of the duel · 2013

Five buttons decide it

You only need these to follow the fight. They describe Zed as he worked in 2013.

R

Death Mark

Zed goes untargetable for about three-quarters of a second, dashes to an enemy and marks them. Three seconds later the mark detonates for damage that grows with everything Zed hit them for in the meantime. A shadow stays where he cast it.

R²

Swap back

Recast the ultimate to trade places with that shadow. It's the only exit once you've dashed in.

QSS

Quicksilver Sash

An item active that removes every debuff on you, including a Death Mark that hasn't detonated yet and an Ignite that's still burning.

IGN

Ignite

True damage over five seconds, plus a cut to healing. On a low-health target it usually finishes the kill.

FL

Flash

A short instant blink. Both players have one, and both will use it.

The outplay, beat by beat

Act I

The trap

Ryu wins the opening exchange as cleanly as a Zed can.

01

Home turf

Thirty-two minutes in, SKT are pushing into KT's base, up 19–9 in kills. Ryu's Zed waits inside the base at almost full health. Faker is about to walk into him.

Ryu has the position, the health and the initiative. Faker has to come to him.

02

Ryu strikes first

Ryu · full shadow combo

The moment Faker steps in, Ryu goes at him. The twin vortices are Zed's shadow-swap effect, and in about a second Ryu burns most of his energy bar on a full combo.

In a mirror match, the first clean combo usually decides the fight.

03

Two-thirds gone

The cyan bolts are Shockblade Zed's shurikens, and they keep landing. Between 32:00.3 and 32:02.3 Faker drops from full health to about a third. Ryu is barely scratched.

After the opening trade Faker is down about two-thirds of his health and Ryu has lost almost none. On paper, the duel is over.

04

Ignite: the kill is set

Ryu · Ignite 32:02.8

Ryu Ignites him. That's the red marker over Faker's health bar: five seconds of true damage, with healing cut. Faker is low, burning, and Ryu still has his ultimate. This is how a Zed closes out a kill.

The usual options here both end in death. Flash away and the burn plus Ryu's ultimate finish you; swing back and Ryu's ultimate does. Faker takes neither.

Act II

Death Mark for Death Mark

Both Zeds commit their ultimates within a second of each other.

05

Faker vanishes

Faker · Death Mark 32:03.3

Faker casts Death Mark on Ryu and his health bar disappears. For about three-quarters of a second he's untargetable and mid-dash, so Ryu has nothing to hit. His shadow stays behind where he cast it.

Here the ultimate works as a dodge first and damage second. It buys time and lights a three-second fuse on Ryu.

06

Marked

Faker reappears behind Ryu and the red slash of Death Mark lands. The fuse is lit: every hit Faker lands on Ryu in the next three seconds is added to the detonation.

Faker's damage is now on a timer that Ryu can't stop by trading back.

07

Ryu answers in kind

Ryu · Death Mark 32:04.0

Ryu reacts almost instantly. Roughly a tenth of a second after Faker becomes targetable again, he Death Marks him straight back. This time Ryu's health bar is the one missing, because he's mid-dash. The crimson swirl is the tail of Faker's own ultimate.

Both Zeds have now committed their ultimates. Two fuses are about to burn at once.

08

Two fuses

Ryu lands in a strike of blue lightning and marks Faker. Both Zeds now carry a Death Mark. Faker's detonates on Ryu at 32:07.0. Ryu's detonates on Faker at about 32:07.9, and at under a quarter health, with Ignite still burning, Faker can't survive it.

Faker cast first, so his fuse finishes first, but only if he's still alive when it does.

Act III

The escape

Two seconds in which Faker removes every way Ryu had to kill him.

09

The swap

Faker · R² swap 32:05.1

About two-tenths of a second after Ryu's mark lands, Faker recasts his ultimate and swaps back to the shadow he left behind, out of Ryu's reach. Ryu is left standing in the vortex where Faker had been. Faker still takes a chunk on the way out and drops to 11%.

Every hit Ryu lands from now on makes his own detonation bigger. Faker takes himself out of range of those hits.

10

Quicksilver

Faker · Quicksilver Sash 32:05.7Ryu · R² swap 32:05.8

Then comes the silver sphere. Faker activates Quicksilver Sash and every debuff on him is gone in one click: Ryu's Death Mark and Ryu's Ignite. From here to the end of the fight, Faker's health line in the chart stays flat at 11%. Ryu, still carrying Faker's mark, swaps back to his own shadow.

He waited until Ryu's mark had actually landed. Cleanse earlier and there's nothing to remove. Cleanse later and he's living tick to tick on the Ignite.

11

The tables turn

Faker · Ignite 32:06.0

Ryu is still wearing Faker's mark, and that's the red orb on him. Faker Ignites him and keeps hitting. Over the next half-second Ryu falls from 74% to 41%, and the damage Faker deals now is added to the mark.

Now Ryu is the one who's burning and marked, with his ultimate already spent.

12

Flash out

Faker · Flash 32:06.5

Faker Flashes away. On 11% health there's no reason to trade even one more auto-attack, because the fuse will do the work.

The hardest part of an outplay is knowing when to stop. With the damage already banked in the mark, Faker steps away.

Act IV

The fuse

One mark detonates. The other was cleansed two seconds earlier.

13

Detonation

Three seconds after it landed, Faker's Death Mark goes off in a white flash. Ryu drops from 41% to 117 of 1,930 HP, about 6%, per his own HUD. Faker's Ignite is still ticking on him.

Without the Quicksilver, Ryu's mark would have gone off on Faker less than a second from now.

14

Last stand

Ryu · Flash 32:07.5

On 117 HP with Ignite burning, Ryu uses his last tool and Flashes right on top of Faker for one final trade.

It's the right desperation play. The Ignite will kill him anyway, so his only hope is to take Faker with him.

15

Slain

Faker · kill 32:08.0

Faker slips out of the lunge, and red Shadow Slashes ring both him and his shadow. Ryu falls at 32:08. Kill gold (+300g) pops over Faker, the kill score goes to 20–9, and Faker walks away on 11% health.

Same champion, same summoner spells, and Ryu started the fight with a 60-point health lead. The difference was the order Faker did things in.

Why it's so impressive

Six things in nine seconds

I

He was already losing

By 32:02.3 Faker was at about a third of his health against a near-full Ryu, with Ignite on him and Ryu's ultimate still up. Nearly every normal response from here ends in a death.

II

The ultimate as a shield

His Death Mark wasn't a burst attempt. It bought about 0.75 s of untargetability and started a timer, so his damage was locked in before he'd committed his escape tools.

III

A two-tenths reaction

Ryu's counter-mark landed at 32:04.9. Faker swapped out at 32:05.1, so Ryu couldn't keep hitting him and load extra damage onto his own detonation.

IV

One click, two answers

A single Quicksilver removed both lethal threats, the Death Mark and the Ignite. Ryu's ultimate and his summoner spell were wiped at once, and Faker's health never moved again.

V

Discipline at 11%

With the fight turned, he didn't chase. He Ignited, landed his damage, Flashed away, and let the fuse finish it.

VI

The stage

A 17-year-old in his first season, in the deciding game of a final, in a mirror match against KT's star mid. SKT won the series 3–2, and this clip made Faker a name for Western audiences.

How this was reconstructed

Frames come from the 1080p broadcast upload (YouTube, ZPCfoCVCx3U) and were sampled at up to 30 fps. Spell timings were read from the cooldown icons in the broadcast side panels (both ultimates and their recasts, both Ignites, Faker's Flash) and from Ryu's on-screen HUD (his Flash, 117/1,930 HP). Health curves come from side-panel bar pixels. Tenths of a second on the game clock are interpolated from frame timing (±0.1 s).

Two calls rest on in-game visual effects rather than HUD readouts, because Faker's item bar isn't on screen: the silver cleanse sphere (Quicksilver Sash; some write-ups say Mercurial Scimitar, which has the same active) and the closing red Shadow Slash. The cleanse is backed up by the data: Faker's Ignite marker disappears at the same moment, and his health never drops again, even though Ryu's mark was due to detonate.
